h: Shabbos Refines the Omer Through the Fire of Holiness

p: "And you shall count for yourselves from the morrow of the Shabbos, etc.:
seven complete Shabbosos shall there be" (Vayikra 23:15).
It does not say "seven complete weeks,"
as it says in parshas Re'eh (Devarim 16:9):
"Seven weeks shall you count for yourself."
that the essence of the counting
which is to purify us of our kelipos
for which we were commanded to count
as we find at the time of Creation,
וַיַּרְא אֱלֹהִים אֶת כָּל אֲשֶׁר עָשָׂה
"And God saw all that He had made,
and behold, it was very good;
And this is expounded in Bereishis Rabbah (9:4)
as referring to everything that is the opposite of good;
if only you would find favor before Me
just as you have found favor before Me
And this was at the time of the addition to Shabbos,
who knows its times, its moments and its hours,
entered into it by a hair's breadth,
and that was the time of the addition to Shabbos,
all the works of the six days,
and after it the six weekdays:
that is, it rectifies all the weekdays.
and three days that precede Shabbos,
into all six days that come after Shabbos.
And likewise it refines the weekdays
before it and those after it,
within the days of the counting.
corresponds to the trait of chessed:
it is to refine the trait of love and longings,
that the traits not be of this world.
"No leaven shall be found in your houses,"
that there be no "leaven in the dough."
And the Sages saw fit to forbid
even the eighth day with chametz;
and all seven days of the counting of chessed
are forbidden with leaven and chametz,
so that there not be found in us
which is the leaven in the dough,
which was the beginning of the corruption.
And for this is the refinement on Shabbos,
and it refines all the days in the trait of chessed.
which is the trait of gevurah:
that is, to empty out all the evil
from "the heart of the fool at his left."
which are the root of the three sins:
עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה גִּלּוּי עֲרָיוֹת וּשְׁפִיכוּת דָּמִים
and all three of them are fire.
is stated explicitly in the verse (Esther 1:12):
And regarding the kelipah of desire we also find
נְפִיק מִינֵּיהּ כִּי עַמּוּדָא דְּנוּרָא וְכוּלֵּי
"It went out of him like a pillar of fire, etc."
And in a pasuk too it is said
like an oven heated by the baker, etc."
And according to what we have said,
which was the first incitement of the serpent:
and regarding idolatry we also find
went out and came like a fiery lion cub
from the Holy of Holies, etc.
And for this is the refinement
in this week of the trait of gevurah,
שֶׁהוּא לְבַטֵּל אֵשׁ שֶׁל יֵצֶר הָרָע
which is to nullify the fire of the yetzer hara
And Shabbos is shin and bas,
the Daughter who is crowned with the Avos,
as is written in the holy Zohar
And it is stated in the holy Zohar
That is, all the Avos are called fire.
although his was the trait of love,
"The seed of Avraham who loved Me,"
and he was a chariot for the trait of chessed
nevertheless at the tenth trial it is written
עַתָּה יָדַעְתִּי כִּי יְרֵא אֱלֹקִים אַתָּה
"Now I know that you fear God."
and this is "I feared out of my joy"
(כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּסֵדֶר אֵלִיָּהוּ רַבָּה רֵישׁ פֶּרֶק ג)
(as stated in Seder Eliyahu Rabbah, beginning of chapter 3).
And regarding love too we find
"For love is strong as death, etc.;
its flashes are flashes of fire,
his trait was "the Fear of Yitzchak" (Bereishis 31:42),
and he was a chariot for the trait of gevurah,
And of Yaakov Avinu too we find
"And the house of Yaakov shall be fire."
And therefore all the Avos are called fire,
and this is "ashishos — these are the Avos."
And as they said in Midrash Rabbah
the fire above and the fire below, etc.;
it explains ashishos from the word esh, fire.
And they correspond to these three kelipos.
the trait of chessed and love,
corresponds to the kelipah of jealousy,
which is the kelipah of Esav,
שֶׁהוּא שׂוֹנֵא דָּמוֹ שֶׁל אָדָם בְּגוּפוֹ
who hates the blood of a person within his body,
while of Avraham Avinu, alav hashalom, it is said
you love to justify My creatures, etc."
the trait of "the Fear of Yitzchak,"
corresponds to the kelipah of desire.
And of Yaakov Avinu it is written
מִי יָקוּם יַעֲקֹב כִּי קָטֹן הוּא
"How shall Yaakov stand, for he is small?"
וְכָל מָקוֹם שֶׁנִּזְכַּר דַּל עָנִי וְאֶבְיוֹן
And wherever "poor, afflicted and needy" is mentioned,
and this corresponds to the kelipah of pride and honor
and all three are fire, as has been said.
when a Jew attains through the three meals
the holiness of the three Avos,
he is able to be refined through the trait of gevurah,
to prevail, to be fire consuming the fire
of the yetzer hara of the three kelipos,
which are called fire, as has been said;
